title: tiered-reserve-controller-with-degradation-stabilizer
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally experience short-term service degradation during headroom exhaustion and rapid decommit cycles. Existing soft-reservation strategies smooth capacity but can oscillate when multiple tenants simultaneously reclaim credits. This PR introduces a Tiered Reserve Controller (TRC) that classifies reservations into three lanes (critical, elastic, opportunistic) and a Degradation Stabilizer that applies an observed-degradation penalty and time-decayed dampening to autoscaler decisions.

What this PR does: Implements TRC core reconciliation logic, integrates with the fleet admission controller, emits new telemetry for per-lane utilization and effective headroom, and provides an opt-in feature flag for gradual rollout. The stabilizer computes a degradation_score from p95 latency regressions and error-rate spikes and reduces the aggressiveness of immediate scale-downs as a function of the score and a configured half-life.

Design notes: The TRC keeps a small in-memory ledger of active reservations and maps them to lanes based on SLA tags and tenant commitment. Lane rules: critical (SLA-backed, no preemption), elastic (committed but preemptible under sustained degradation), opportunistic (best-effort, first to shed). The Degradation Stabilizer uses a lightweight EWMA over 1m/5m windows and a configurable multiplier to adjust target_desired_replicas. We prioritized a controller-side implementation (vs. control-plane-only) to keep decision surface near the allocator and to allow future on-host hedging.

Telemetry and observability: Added metrics: trc_lane_utilization{lane}, trc_lane_headroom{lane}, trc_degradation_score, trc_stabilizer_adjustment, trc_shed_actions_total. Traces annotate reconciliation spans with lane decisions and adjustment factors. Dashboard and alert runbook updates are included in README changes.

Backward compatibility and safety: Default behavior is off; when enabled, TRC runs in dry-run mode for N reconciliations (configurable) before applying actions. Feature flag: redwood.trc.enabled and redwood.trc.stabilizer.half_life_seconds. Existing reservation API remains unchanged; lane assignment is derived server-side from known commitment tiers.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests cover lane assignment, adjustment math, and reconciliation edge cases. Integration tests simulate bursty reclaim scenarios against the autoscaler harness. Performance microbenchmarks show controller CPU + mem increase <5% under typical load. Rollout plan: enable for 5% of fleets with monitoring, then gradual 25/50/100% after two-day stability windows.

Related: ENG-1987 describes customer incidents motivating a soft-hedging mechanism; ENG-2041 tracks observability gaps discovered during the incident postmortem.

Checklist: - [x] Controller logic implemented - [x] Telemetry emitted and documented - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Feature-flag gating - [x] Runbook and dashboard notes
